steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Stir in onion; cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.

Place diced potatoes, water, carrots, and chicken bouillon in another large pot; bring to a boil. Cook until vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes. Do not overcook. Season with black pepper to taste.
Add flour to cooked onions; stir constantly until a paste forms, about 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until warmed through.
Add potato-carrot mixture, parsley, and thyme. Continue cooking until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: This old-fashioned potato soup recipe is easy to make with tender potatoes, onions, butter, and milk for a creamy, comforting, and versatile soup.
raw_recipe.name: Old-Fashioned Potato Soup

review.reviewBody: Made this on a day when comfort food was what I wanted and it filled the bill admirably. Changed the method a bit, though because having to wash two stockpots would have made it that much less comforting. Cooked the onion, as directed, then added the potatoes and carrots to the onion, sauteed for about 5 minutes on medium low heat, added vegetable broth, brought to a boil, and then simmered, covered, for about 15 minutes, till potatoes were tender. Added herbs and pepper, and 2 cups of milk. Whisked flour with the other cup of milk, and added it to the simmering soup. Cooked till thickened. Served bowls of grated cheese and crumbled bacon (for the meat eaters in the family) on the side, and some lovely cheese toast. Felt much better afterward. Thanks so much.

This has become my little black dress of creamy soups and it's never failed me. It's a solid base that you can accessorize however you wish. The first time I made this I sauteed with olive oil rather than butter, and I replaced water for whey leftover from making cheese (with non-fat powdered milk, no less). It was hands-down the best potato soup I've ever had, and not a soul would believe it didn't have butter (and lots of fat) in it. Even better the second time around. 

Realize here that you're making a roux - if you don't know about roux it's worth looking up so you understand how it works.

I also didn’t want to wash two pots so after I cooked the onion in the butter, I added the potatoes (I was in a hurry and didn’t peel them-used mini potatoes), chicken bone broth and let that simmer (added salt and pepper) for 10-15min. Then I added the flour, milk, and herbs. Let it cook until it thickened a bit. Added a little garlic and cheese. It’s amazing and turned out great for such a quick recipe.

Some people are saying they made this in one pot. If you want your soup thick, you need to make it as stated in the recipe. The roux thickens the soup to a typical potato soup consistency. I made this for my mom who is battling cancer and not many foods taste good to her. She adores it! I just made her a second batch to freeze and heat up as needed. I added garlic to the onions (cancer fighter), subbed bone broth for bullion (better for gut health), used whole milk for extra calories, and subbed a bag of precut potatoes mixed with peppers and onions to simplify the prep time.

Turned out great. I changed things up as I always do. I added bacon and cooked the onions and fresh garlic in the bacon gease with the butter. Had add an extra tbl. Spoon of flour to thicken it. Didn't use water instead used chicken broth . Also used 1/2 cream and the other half milk. Then dumped it in the insta pot for about 20 minutes. Smells awesome cooking. Also making it for tomorrow's dinner I want to let the flavors come together overnight. Planning on making some fresh crusty bread to dunk in it tomorrow night. Delicious.

I took advice from Susiekew: sauted onions, added potatoes to onions, sauted 5 min, added chicken boullion to 3 c boiling water, added to onion/potato in pan, simmered 15 min til potatoes were tender, stirred 2 c milk, brought to simmer, whisked 3 T flour into remaining cup milk, stirred into pan & cooked to thicken. Wasn't thick enough for my taste so put about a cup & a half in the blender & pulsed til mostly smooth, poured it back in the pan. Turned out DELICIOUS. Thanks Susiekew for the tips.

Used 5 carrots, 7 potatoes and 2 onions. We like our soup with plenty of vegetables. Instead of water and bouillon I used 3 cups of chicken stock and used 2 cups of milk mixed with 1 cup of heavy cream. At the end my husband added 1/2 teaspoon chili flakes and it gave it a lovely pop of flavor. Also used a full teaspoon of thyme. It was delicious!

I should have looked at suggestions from this recipe before beginning. I cooked diced onions and celery together in a small skillet (no carrots) with butter. I cooked the potatoes in a 3 quart pot. The potatoes took 13 minutes to cook. I drained the potatoes, and used my immersion blender to mash the potatoes, then I added the onion and celery, 2 cups milk, 1/4 cup half and half and salt and pepper. Really good. Thank you, susiekew for the suggestions and method to make this using one pot. I will do that next time.
My family loved it. I added a1 cup heavy cream and just 2 cups milk and celery and turned out great! Also, added a grilled cheese made with sour dough bread for dipping!🥰😋
I used Garlic butter and onion butter seasoning, added more flavor. I also blended it and served in bread bowls.

This was really good soup! I made it the way susiekew below did because I also like comfort food to be comforting, not a pain to clean up and it turned out splendidly! Maybe I just got lucky because I'm not a great cook but the soup was as creamy as potato soup should be. Being a veghead, I used "Not-Chick'n" bouillon (which is suprisingly chicken-like, from what I remember chicken to be like). I'm keeping this recipe!
Easy to follow recipe and delicious! Will make again!
Love how it was easy to make! Whole family enjoyed it

I made this! I changed it up though! I used heavy whipping cream instead of milk. I added a half a stick of butter to the potatoes and carrot mixture. I added sage, rosemary garlic, and garlic salt as well as the herbs it suggested. I added bacon pieces and my family loves cheese! It was delicious
I even add smoked sausage to it.
This tasted really good. I didn't add any cheese and I didn't put as much milk as they wanted. I did add celery instead of carrots. It was fantastic and my husband who doesn't like soup ate it.
I really enjoyed this soup. I made half of a recipe and it worked beautifully. I served it with cheddar cheese and YUMMY!!! So good!
You can really tell the difference between a potato soup I usually make and this one, This might be easy but it's not flavorful like the one I make. Never again I'll stick to my own recipe.
Use skim milk to lower fat content.
Thanks for this recipe. It was easy for me to make.
